verdict.rationale: Unreal has broad first-party API documentation for C++ gameplay programming, delegates and reflection macros, Python editor scripting, and the Remote Control HTTP/WebSocket APIs, and those docs can be fetched keylessly. Several things undercut LLM first-try success, though. Source access is EULA- and account-gated, so the GitHub repo returns Not Found to anonymous clients and public code examples are harder to come by. llms.txt exists but is intermittently blocked by 403 challenges. Community reports say engine version upgrades break things ('everything breaks'), which points to API instability. Missing for 10: any direct evidence that LLM-generated Unreal code works on the first try, evidence of API stability across versions, openly accessible source and example code, and reliable machine-readable doc access.
